title: Family jokes, family rules
description: Every family runs on two invisible documents: the rules nobody wrote down and the jokes nobody else understands.

body.heading: The jokes are the archive
paragraphs: The story of the disastrous holiday, the nickname with a twenty-year pedigree, the phrase that reduces the whole table to helplessness — these are not decorations on family life. They are its archive: proof, retold annually, that you have a shared past and survived it together.
Tell them in front of the children, even the ones too young to understand. They are learning the shape of belonging before they learn the content.

body.heading: Rules work better when they are few
paragraphs: Unwritten family rules — we do not shout at the table, we always say where we are going, we knock — hold because everyone can recite them. Families rarely need more rules; they need the few real ones kept consistently and the rest released.
It is worth, once in a while, saying the rules out loud together and retiring the dead ones. A rule nobody can explain becomes a superstition, and superstitions breed resentment.

body.heading: Welcome the editors
paragraphs: New partners, grown children, and in-laws will edit both documents — adding jokes, questioning rules. That is not dilution; it is how the archive stays alive. The families that thrive are the ones whose story can absorb new authors.
Keep the pen moving. A family’s documents are never finished, and that is rather the point.

takeaway: Keep the jokes retold, the rules few and explainable, and the documents open to new editors.
